content: Last year at the Simons Foundation Lean workshop we wrote a maximize / minimize tactic: given linear hypothesis, it uses the simplex oracle of linarith to compute the optimal bound on a linear objective. @Heather Macbeth proposed the project, @Siqing Zhang wrote the front end, @Shuli Chen and I wrote the backend, and @Rob Lewis advised it. The work was mostly done but stopped in August 2025, so it falls far behind master. Siqing Zhang and I plan to pick it up to rebase and refine it and then open a pr. The code was on https://github.com/szqzs/mathlib4/pull/2. Before we start working, I'd like to know: is this tactic still wanted in Mathlib?

Code example:

example (x y : ℚ) (h1 : 3 * x + y > -4) (h2 : x > -2) : True := by
  minimize 4 * x + y with H
  -- Creates: have H : -6 ≤ 4 * x + y := by linarith
  trivial

Looks cool! Do you know of use-cases in mathlib? Is it geared towards when you're figuring out a proof for the first time? (Otherwise the formalizer already knows the bound I guess)

"Is it geared towards when you're figuring out a proof for the first time?" mostly yes, If I remember correctly (@Heather Macbeth please correct me if I got wrong) the motivation of the project is indeed for exploring the constant directly through interaction with lean rather than needing to copy the constraint out to something like Walfram Alpha. (btw this won't interrupt the proof process as it add H to context) I'm not sure if there would be current use-cases in mathlib, I personally think it's more like a dev tool.
Then perhaps it makes more sense to name it minimize? and then it can suggest a Try this: with the have bound?

It does print something like Try this: have H : 4 * x + y ≤ 6 := by linarith (through addSuggestion and evalTactic) ; as for naming it minimize?, I'm less sure. The ? tactics that I know of (apply?, exact?, e.t.c.) are goal-directed, whereas for the usage of this tactic the user needs to feed in the linear objective and it does not search over the goal. But I don't have strong feeling about the naming.
Regarding naming, we also used to have the polyrith tactic which was also self-replacing. I think it's fine to have minimize be another such tactic, and don't think a question mark is required.
Thanks both! I'll keep maximize / minimize without the question mark and rebase onto current master, then open a PR. If anyone has concerns, please let me know.

Quick follow-up while rebasing maxmize/minimize: currently the tactic prints its bound as a numeral (have: 4 * x + y ≤ 7 / 2 := by linarith) using the Quote ℤ / Quote ℚ instances from Mathlib/Tactic/Polyrith.lean, which have been removed together with polyrith.

I think Quote ℤ / Quote ℚ would be generally useful so I'd like to restore them in the pr, but I'm not sure where to put them--Quote Nat lives in Init/Meta/Defs.lean, which is not part of Mathlib. Is a Mathlib file (e.g. under Mathlib/Util/) acceptable, or would people prefer this go to core? Or, if this global instance is not wanted, I can just add a local helper def ratToTerm (q : ℚ) : MetaM Term.

Is a Mathlib file (e.g. under Mathlib/Util/) acceptable

Putting some code into mathlib (before possibly submitting it to Lean core) certainly is acceptable.

Follow-up: I opened #44786 to restore Quote ℤ and Quote ℚ. It's relatively small (around 10 lines for Quote ℤ and Quote ℚ and 121 lines for tests) and self-contained. Would anyone have time to review it? Thanks!

I'll continue refining the maximize/minimizebased on them.

While preparing the maximize/minimize PR, I found that @Kim Morrison's leanprover/lp also has a maximize tactic. The main differences:

  1. lp is a separate package (with a SoPlex backend by default); ours would be in Mathlib with no extra dependency.
  2. Ours also has minimize, gives a clickable "Try this" suggestion, and produces strict < bounds when provable, whereas lp's adds hbound : e ≤ N.
  3. Ours reuses linarith's preprocessing and simplex oracle; lp has its own preprocessing and certificate-based proof construction.

Kim, do you think a Mathlib PR for this is still worthwhile, or would this kind of work be better contributed to lp?
